World’s Second-Largest Hardware Wallet Maker Trezor Warns of Suspected Hardware Implant in Device Sold by Reseller Trezor said it received a credible report of a suspected hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device purchased from reseller CryptoBilis in August 2026. The company has not yet received the device for verification, and no CryptoBilis customer has reported losing funds. Trezor urged customers who purchased devices from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to move their funds to newly created wallets with new recovery seeds as soon as possible. The company removed CryptoBilis as a reseller on October 9 following reports of tampered Ledger devices. Four Trezor devices inspected so far showed no signs of tampering, and the investigation remains ongoing. — link

Coinbase Q3 Revenue Falls 35% to $1.22B, Net Profit Rebounds to $719M; Prediction Markets Top $200M Annualized Coinbase reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.22 billion, down 35% year over year, while net income rose 66% to $719 million, ending three consecutive quarters of losses. Earnings per share reached $2.51, with profits largely driven by unrealized crypto gains. Adjusted net income was $78 million. Meanwhile, prediction markets surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue, with 82% quarterly compound growth since launch. Coinbase's crypto trading market share reached 10.7%, while average USDC holdings hit a record $22 billion. — link

Binance Reserves Over $6.34B in Company Funds to Cover Hack Losses, Including $5B in Affected Tokens Binance said it has reserved over $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from the hack, including $5 billion already held in the affected tokens. It is purchasing the remaining tokens through market and OTC channels, a process that may take longer due to limited liquidity. The reserved funds are separate from approximately $3 billion in frozen assets. Binance will publicly verify user assets through its Proof of Reserves. — link

Coinbase Executives Plan Potential Sale of Up to 13.6M COIN Shares Worth $2.2B According to Coinbase's Q3 SEC filing, CEO Brian Armstrong, co-founder Fred Ehrsam, and President Emilie Choi adopted Rule 10b5-1 trading plans allowing potential sales of up to 13.6 million COIN shares, worth approximately $2.2 billion based on the October 29 closing price. Armstrong's plan covers up to 8.17 million shares between November 16, 2026, and October 2027, subject to predetermined price thresholds. These are planned transactions, not completed sales. — link
